doc.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Boston youth and learning the bass
title: Studying bass with Fred Zimmermann
summary: He studied privately with Zimmermann for about seven years; Zimmermann was not a jazz player but supportive, and recommended him for The Bell Telephone Hour.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So you worked on the technique of the bass with him. And your jazz playing, was that something you worked on with him or was that more self-taught?

Well I did jazz playing, not so much with him, no. He had a feel for it. You know he was with the Philharmonic and he taught at Juilliard during that period. He wasn’t a jazz player but he was loose. He was a good golfer, he was a marvelous painter, and he loved the bass, he adored the bass. And he was just — I studied privately and he taught at Juilliard but I just studied privately with him. And as time went on he was very kind to me and I used to come in evenings and he’d play duets with me and things like that. And then eventually he even sent me to, he recommended me to take his place with “The Bell Telephone Hour” — he was playing on that show. Donald Voorhees was the conductor, I don’t know, you wouldn’t have remembered it, but you’ll find they were all NBC.
